analysis:
Examined units: ProviderLoop+ModelLoading.swift head 1044-1689 and ProviderLoop+Serve.swift base 1-603, plus the Serve patch. Per the range map, ModelLoading head 1044-1689 is unchanged; the edits are at head 47-78 and 542-658, outside these units. Those edits route weight hashing through an injectable loadWeightHasher and add managed GLM manifest SHA-256 verification.

The only Serve change is head line 108: `if usesHostServices { verifiedWeightHashesFile = VerifiedWeightHashStore.path() }`. This arms a new persisted, host-only verified-weight-hash store, armed alongside loaded-models persistence. The store is new on-disk state under operator control (TB-003). VerifiedWeightHashStore and its readers/writers are not in these units.

Integration must check whether persisted hashes are ever trusted instead of recomputing/re-verifying weights at load. If so, an operator (ADV-001) could edit the file or swap weights after verification to keep a stale verified hash. That hash would flow to liveModelHashes, loadedModelHashesSnapshot (head 1199-1205), syncWarmModelState currentModelHash (1217), registration/heartbeat model hashes and challenge responses. This bears on T-012, T-027 and A-004. The persisted hash also feeds the SSD prefix-cache weightHash binding (T-041, mitigation 'verified weightHash in coordinator mode'). A stale persisted hash could let cache entries from different weights be adopted.

Weight hashes are already provider-self-reported, so this may not regress the trust model. That holds only if the store is keyed by a snapshot fingerprint (path/size/mtime/inode) and invalidated on mismatch. Also verify the store's file permissions, symlink handling (no-follow), atomic writes and parse fail-closed behavior.

The unchanged unload, eviction, admission (fastAdmissionReject) and loadErrorStatusCode paths showed no security-relevant change. Registration attestation (base 579-601) is unchanged. No concrete regression is supported from the visible evidence.
